## a2e752ad6948

**Finding: possible lesson-window shortcut, reproduced.** Generator SHA-256
`7449bbd641263736246fab96a870367355390e48e6ab392a3a75ad014eecbc34`;
selected rule hash `39fb0a2b12e8`.

At difficulty `medium`, seed 120, generated samples 0, 1 and 2 contain two frames
each, and all six frame-interior top-left cells have global parity 1. Therefore
the wrong rule “inside every frame, put marker color where `(row+column)%2==1`
and border color on parity 0” exactly matches the authoritative Racket outputs
for all three demonstrations. The next generated sample (index 3) has frame
origin parities `[0, 1]`; the same rival disagrees with authority on six cells.
All four inputs pass the target validator, and the target declares neither
`EXAMPLES_NEEDED`, a schedule contract, nor semantic rivals that would detect
this window.

Evidence:

- `checks/audit/a2e752ad6948/scan.json` records seed, indices, observed controls,
  origin parities and zero validator errors;
- `lesson_inputs.json` contains the four exact generated inputs;
- `racket.json` is the supported source-bound Racket execution receipt;
- `counterexample.json` includes the index-3 input, actual Racket output, rival
  output, six differing cells, hashes, command and working directory;
- `rival_outputs.json` records `[true, true, true, false]` authority agreement.

This is a **possible training shortcut**, not a claim that the production
sampler always assembles exactly indices 0–2 as demonstrations and index 3 as
query. The reproducible risk is that unscheduled three-example windows can all
share one global origin parity. A repair would schedule both global origin
parities within every lesson and declare the global-parity rival; no audit-target
source was changed here.

## a2e752ad6948

**Finding type: possible lesson-window shortcut, independently reproduced.** No source was changed. Generator SHA-256 `7449bbd641263736246fab96a870367355390e48e6ab392a3a75ad014eecbc34`; selected rule hash `39fb0a2b12e8`.

At difficulty `medium`, seed `120`, generated samples 0, 1, and 2 each contain two frames whose interior top-left cells all have global parity 1. Therefore the wrong rule **“inside each frame, put marker color wherever `(row + column) % 2 == 1`, and border color on parity 0”** exactly matches the selected Racket outputs for all three demonstrations. Sample 3 has frame-origin parities `[0,1]`; the same rival disagrees with authority on six cells. All four inputs pass the target validator and are ordinary generator outputs.

Evidence: `checks/audit/a2e752ad6948/scan.json`, `lesson_inputs.json`, `racket.json`, `rival_outputs.json`, and `counterexample.json`.

This reproduces the task’s prior unresolved audit lead against the unchanged current source rather than relying on the historical report. It is a possible three-demonstration-window defect, not a claim that every production assembler chooses exactly samples 0–2 as demos and 3 as query. A repair would schedule both global frame-origin parities within every allowed lesson and declare this rival in an executable semantic contract.
